title: Finite étale splitting of a torus over an affine normal Noetherian base
statement: Let $S$ be an affine normal Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme] [pqf-def-locnoeth] [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], where normal means that every local ring is a normal domain. Here Noetherian means locally Noetherian and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. For any scheme $U$, define $\mathbf G_{m,U}$ by gluing $\operatorname{Spec}A[t,t^{-1}]$ over affine opens $\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq U$, with multiplication, unit and inverse induced by $t\mapsto t\otimes t$, $t\mapsto1$, and $t\mapsto t^{-1}$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] [def-weil-laurent-polynomial-ring]. An $S$-group scheme here means a group object in $S$-schemes, with multiplication, inverse and unit morphisms satisfying the group identities. Let $T$ be such a group scheme which is fppf locally isomorphic to $\mathbf G_{m,S}^r$, with finite locally constant rank $r\geq0$ [def-pc-fppf-site]. Then $T\to S$ is affine, smooth and of finite presentation [pqf-def-affine-morphism] [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. There exists a finite étale surjection $u:S'\to S$ [def-weil-etale-morphism] [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] [def-weil-surjective-morphism], hence a finite flat locally finitely presented surjection [def-pc-finite-locally-free], such that $S'$ is a finite disjoint union of normal integral affine Noetherian schemes $S'_j$ [def-pc-integral-scheme], and $T\times_SS'_j\simeq\mathbf G_{m,S'_j}^{r_j}$ as group schemes for every $j$. The empty base and rank zero are allowed. Fibre products use [def-pc-fibre-product], and finite presentation uses [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions].

source.place: Appendix A.1.3 (tori) and A.1.8 (isotriviality over locally Noetherian geometrically unibranch bases), arXiv:2201.06424v4, printed pp.50–52; affine Noetherian specialization. WANTED local copy. Normality and finite component refinements are part of the stated specialization.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finite-components], $S$ has finitely many irreducible components. Every quasi-compact open has finitely many components as well: it is a quasi-compact open of a locally Noetherian scheme, hence Noetherian. Apply [lem-sfb-normal-locally-finite-components] to obtain a finite disjoint clopen decomposition $S=\coprod_a S_a$ into normal integral schemes. Each $S_a$ is Noetherian: it is locally Noetherian as an open, and quasi-compact as a closed subset of quasi-compact $S$. If $S$ is empty take $S'=S$ and the identity; all assertions are vacuous. Otherwise it suffices to construct a finite etale splitting cover of each nonempty $S_a$ and take their disjoint union. Each $S_a$ is connected because it is integral.

First $T$ is commutative: multiplication and multiplication after swapping the factors agree on the given fppf splitting cover. On each affine test scheme the cover admits a finite affine fppf refinement by [lem-pc-fppf-affine-refinement]; its finite disjoint union is an fpqc cover. Uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent] tests equality of the two maps there, hence globally. Apply [lem-sfb-relative-torus-character-reconstruction] to $T$. It gives the etale lattice sheaf $M=X^*(T)$, the isomorphism $T\simeq D_S(M)$ and arbitrary base-change compatibility. Its structure-map clause proves that $T\to S$ is affine, smooth and of finite presentation. On each connected $S_a$ the locally constant rank of $M$ is a single integer $r_a\geq0$: distinct rank loci are disjoint open subsets whose union is $S_a$. Write $M_a=M|_{S_a}$.

source.place: Appendix A.1.2 (tori), A.1.3 (biduality), A.1.8 (isotriviality); https://arxiv.org/html/2201.06424v4, online text read, local copy WANTED. Reconstruction supplied by the existing relative-character node.

proof.text: On $(S_a)_{\mathrm{et}}$ form the sheaf $P_a$ of bases of $M_a$: a section over $U$ is an isomorphism $\underline{\mathbf Z^{r_a}}|_U\xrightarrow{\sim}M_a|_U$. Maps and their inverses glue uniquely, so this is a sheaf. On an etale chart trivializing $M_a$, $P_a$ is the constant sheaf with value $\operatorname{GL}_{r_a}(\mathbf Z)$. An isomorphism is determined by the images of the finitely many standard basis vectors. By [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-sections-locally-constant], these are Zariski-locally constant integer vectors, hence locally a single matrix; invertibility says that the matrix is in $\operatorname{GL}_{r_a}(\mathbf Z)$. Conversely such a locally constant matrix gives the isomorphism and its inverse. Thus $P_a$ is locally constant and locally nonempty. Its comparison inverse image $F_a=\nu_{S_a}^*P_a$ is locally constant and locally nonempty on $(S_a)_{\mathrm{proet}}$: the same trivializing charts are pro-etale covers by [lem-pur-etale-proetale-cover]; inverse image of [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] preserves constants and local trivializations. This uses finite-limit and colimit preservation: the constant sheaf of a set is a coproduct of terminal sheaves. No finiteness of $\operatorname{GL}_{r_a}(\mathbf Z)$ is asserted.

source.place: Lemma 7.3.9, printed pp.67–68; Lemma 7.4.10 and its proof, printed p.71; application to the sheaf of lattice bases.

proof.text: The scheme $S_a$ is nonempty, connected, normal and Noetherian by step 1. Apply [lem-a1-normal-locally-constant-finite-section] to $F_a$. It supplies a finite etale surjection $v_a:Y_a\to S_a$ and $s_a\in F_a(Y_a)$. By [det-pe-classical-sheaves-unit], $P_a\to\nu_{S_a,*}\nu_{S_a}^*P_a$ is an isomorphism. Direct image here is restriction by [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Evaluating at the etale object $Y_a\to S_a$ therefore gives $F_a(Y_a)=P_a(Y_a)$ canonically. Thus $s_a$ is a basis $\underline{\mathbf Z^{r_a}}\simeq M_a|_{Y_a}$. The base-change and constant-lattice clauses of [lem-sfb-relative-torus-character-reconstruction] give $T\times_S Y_a\simeq\mathbf G_{m,Y_a}^{r_a}$ as group schemes.

source.place: Lemma 7.3.9, printed pp.67–68; Lemma 7.4.10 and its proof, printed p.71; application to the sheaf of lattice bases.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-finite-etale-normal-generic-components] to $Y_a\to S_a$, whose base is normal integral Noetherian. It decomposes $Y_a$ into finitely many clopen normal integral subschemes $Y_{a,j}$. Also $Y_a$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]: a finite morphism is of finite type, since finitely many module generators also generate its algebra; an affine preimage is quasi-compact. Each $Y_{a,j}$ is locally Noetherian as an open and quasi-compact as a closed subset of $Y_a$, hence Noetherian. Form $S'=\coprod_aY_a$ using [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family], with $u$ equal to $v_a$ on each summand. Over the disjoint clopen bases $S_a$, it is the given finite etale surjection, so it is finite etale and surjective over $S$. In particular $S'$ is affine because a finite morphism is affine and $S$ is affine. Each clopen $Y_{a,j}\subset S'$ is affine: by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-clopen-idempotent] its underlying open in $\operatorname{Spec}B=S'$ is $D(e)$ for an idempotent $e$, and its open subscheme is $\operatorname{Spec}B_e$. Restrict the step-4 isomorphism to each component and set $r_{a,j}=r_a$.

proof.text: By [def-weil-etale-morphism], $u$ is flat and locally of finite presentation. Together with finiteness, this is exactly finite local freeness in [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. Surjectivity was proved in step 5. In rank zero the basis sheaf has the single empty basis, the reconstructed group is the trivial group $\mathbf G_m^0$, and the argument applies. For a nonempty base the cover has nonempty fibres; for the empty base use the identity from step 1.
